templates.pattern: Eight persons [P1]-[P8] live on 8 floors (1=ground, 8=top). Each has a different profession and a different car. Professions: Doctor, Engineer, Lawyer, Teacher, CA, Banker, Pilot, Chef. Cars: Alto, Swift, Innova, Verna, Baleno, Creta, Nexon, Brezza. [P1] is a Doctor on floor [F1]. [P3] is 3 floors above [P1] and owns Innova. [P5] is on floor 7 and is a Banker. [P7] is on the top floor and is a Pilot. [P2] is on an even floor between [P1] and [P3] and owns Alto. [P4] is a Lawyer on floor 2. [P6] is directly below [P5] and is a CA. [P8] is on floor 1 and is a Chef. Who is on floor 5 and what is their profession?

Seven persons [P1]-[P7] sit in a circle. Each likes a different day of the week (Mon-Sun) and has a different age between [A1] and [A7] years. [P1] likes Monday, age [A1]. [P3] likes Wednesday, age [A3]. [P5] likes Friday, age [A5]. The person who likes Thursday is 3 years older than [P1]. [P2] is to immediate right of [P1]. Age of person liking Tuesday = ([A1]+[A3])/2. How old is the person who likes Thursday?

Ten persons [P1]-[P10] are split into 2 teams of 5. Team A: [P1],[P2],[P3],[P4],[P5]. Team B: [P6],[P7],[P8],[P9],[P10]. Each person has a unique jersey number 1-10. [P1] wears #[N1]. [P3] wears a number [K] more than [P1]. [P5] wears the highest in Team A. [P7] wears #[N7]. [P9] wears [M] less than [P7]. Sum of Team A jersey numbers = [SA]. What is [P2]'s jersey number?
templates.explanation: [P4] is whatever remains. [P2]=SA-[P1]-[P3]-[P4]-[P5]. Since [P5]=10(highest in A if all taken), [P2]=SA-N1-(N1+K)-10-[P4]. Simplified answer.

templates.pattern: Six couples (12 persons) [P1]-[P12] sit at a rectangular dining table. 3 on each long side, none at ends. [P1] and [P2] are married; no couple sits on the same side. [P1] is on side A, position 2 (middle). [P3] is directly opposite [P1] on side B. [P5] is to the right of [P1] on side A. [P4] is to the left of [P3] on side B. [P7] is directly opposite [P5]. [P8] is to the right of [P3] on side B. [P2] sits on side B. Is [P2] sitting next to [P3]?
templates.explanation: Side B: [P4]-[P3]-[P8]. [P2] must be on side B but [P4],[P3],[P8] fill side B. So [P2] is [P4] — placed to left of [P3]. [P2] IS next to [P3] → Answer: Yes

templates.pattern: Nine persons [P1]-[P9] have different weights (kg). [P1]=[W]kg. [P3] weighs [A]% more than [P1]. [P5] weighs [B]% less than [P3]. [P7] weighs [C]kg more than [P5]. [P9] is the heaviest at [MAX]kg. [P2] weighs exactly between [P1] and [P3]. What is [P7]'s weight?

Eight students [P1]-[P8] appeared in exams across [N] subjects. Each scored different total marks. [P1]=[M1], [P2]=[M1]+[K], [P3]=[M1]+2[K], [P4]=[M1]+3[K]... (arithmetic progression). [P8] scored the most. What is the average score of all 8 students?

Six persons [P1]-[P6] each work on a different project (A-F) and sit in a row. Project durations (months): A=[DA], B=[DB], C=[DC], D=[DD], E=[DE], F=[DF]. [P1] works on Project A and sits at position [POS]. [P3] works on the longest project and sits to the immediate right of [P1]. [P5] works on the shortest project. Sum of durations of projects done by [P1] and [P3] = ?
templates.explanation: [P3] works on longest project = Project C (DC). [P1]+[P3] = DA+DC = [DA]+[DC]

templates.pattern: Ten items [I1]-[I10] are arranged in 2 rows of 5. Row 1 (top): [I1]-[I5] left to right. Row 2 (bottom): [I6]-[I10] left to right. Each item has a unique price. [I1]=Rs.[P1]. [I3]=Rs.[P3]. [I6] is directly below [I1] and costs [K]% more than [I1]. [I8] is directly below [I3] and costs [M]% less than [I3]. [I5] is the most expensive at Rs.[P5]. [I10] is the cheapest. What is the combined price of [I6] and [I8]?

Seven employees [P1]-[P7] joined a company in different years [Y1]-[Y7]. Each has a different experience level and salary. [P1] joined in [Y1] with salary Rs.[S1]K. For every year of experience (current year [CY] minus joining year), salary increases by Rs.[INC]K. [P3] joined [K] years after [P1]. [P5] joined [M] years after [P3]. What is [P5]'s current salary?
templates.explanation: [P5] joined year = Y1+K+M. Experience = CY-(Y1+K+M). Salary = S1 + experience*INC

templates.pattern: Eight persons [P1]-[P8] sit around a circular table. Each has a different nationality and a different hobby. Nationalities: Indian, Chinese, American, British, French, German, Japanese, Russian. Hobbies: Chess, Reading, Painting, Cooking, Gardening, Swimming, Cycling, Photography. [P1] is Indian and likes Chess. [P3] is British and likes Painting; sits opposite [P1]. [P5] is American, likes Cooking; sits 3rd to right of [P1]. [P7] is Japanese, likes Photography; sits between [P5] and [P3]. [P2] is French; sits to immediate right of [P1]. [P4] likes Gardening; sits between [P2] and [P3]. What is [P4]'s nationality?

Six students [P1]-[P6] take [N] tests. Scores follow a pattern: [P1]'s score in test [T] = [BASE]+[STEP]*T. [P1]'s scores: Test1=[SC1], Test2=[SC2], Test3=[SC3]. [P2]'s total = [P1]'s total + [K]. [P3]'s total = [P2]'s total - [M]. What is the average of [P1],[P2],[P3] totals?

Nine persons [P1]-[P9] are arranged in a 3x3 matrix. Positions: (row,col). [P1] is at (1,1). [P5] is at centre (2,2). [P9] is at (3,3). [P3] is at (1,3). [P7] is at (3,1). The sum of values in each row and column is equal (magic square). Values are [V1]-[V9]. [P1]=[V1],[P5]=[V5],[P9]=[V9]. Row1 sum=[P1]+[P2]+[P3]=[RS]. What is [P2]'s value?

Seven persons [P1]-[P7] each boarded a different train at times [T1]-[T7]. Each train goes to a different city. [P1] boarded at [T1] hrs going to City A. [P3] boarded [K] minutes after [P1]. [P5] boarded [M] minutes before [P3]. [P7] boarded last at [T7]. Time between [P1] and [P7] is [D] minutes. How many minutes after [P1] did [P5] board?
templates.explanation: [P3] boards at T1+K. [P5] boards at [P3]-M = T1+K-M. Minutes after [P1] = K-M = [K]-[M]
